desc: Implement the full Python program using the antipodal quotient: aggregate row masks with their complements into a frequency array of size 1<<(W-1), build g[i]=min(i.bit_count(), W-i.bit_count()), compute the XOR convolution with three in-place integer FWHTs, and print min(result)//N.
Handle W=1 correctly (answer 0) and ensure the inverse FWHT division is exact integer division; final program reads stdin and writes stdout only.
Validate on the provided samples and small random brute-force cases; all 3 public samples passed.
No fallback needed; the O(H + W*2^(W-1)) three-FWHT solution is within constraints for W <= 18.
